component.noPage: The kit has no page for "{slug}".

alert.aNoteAtTheHead: A note at the head of a page or a card: something the reader should know before going on. It stays until its cause is gone — for a passing message use a toast.
alert.whatCanBeDoneAbout: What can be done about it stands at the end, the quiet action first.
alert.aFewStrongWordsBefore: A few strong words before the text.
alert.howAScreenReaderAnnounces: How a screen reader announces it.
alert.twoPluginsWaitForYour: Two plugins wait for your approval.
alert.twoPluginsWaitForYour2: Two plugins wait for your approval. They stay off until an admin approves them.

avatar.aPersonOrAThing: A person, or a thing with a name, as a small square: its picture, or its initial when it has none.
avatar.inATableCellThe: In a table cell the avatar is `xsmall` and stands 8px before the name.
avatar.theInitialShownWhenThere: The initial shown when there is no picture.
avatar.thePictureAndWhatIt: The picture and what it shows.
avatar.sixSizesFromATable: Six sizes, from a table cell to a profile.

badge.aShortStateBesideA: A short state beside a name. StateBadge — a dot and a word — is a record’s state in a list or a header. Badge — a tinted label — marks something about a thing: a role, a warning, a count.
badge.theToneIsTheOne: The tone is the one the status option declares. Anything else is neutral.
badge.aBadgeFollowsTheName: A badge follows the name it speaks of, 6–8px after it, centred on its line.
badge.successWarningDangerInfoOr: SUCCESS, WARNING, DANGER, INFO or DEFAULT.
badge.theWordOneOrTwo: The word — one or two, in sentence case.

button.whatSomeonePressesToMake: What someone presses to make something happen. One primary button a screen; everything else is secondary or ghost.
button.primaryIsTheOneThing: Primary is the one thing the screen is for. Secondary is every other action. Ghost is an action that should not draw the eye. Danger removes or cannot be undone.
button.theIconGoesInIcon: The icon goes in `icon`, not in the children, so it keeps its gap and gives way to the spinner while loading. Icons are 15px.
button.aSquareOfTheSame: A square of the same height. It has no words, so it must carry an `aria-label`.
button.aLoadingButtonKeepsIts: A loading button keeps its width, shows a spinner and cannot be pressed again. A disabled one says the action is not available now.
button.aButtonThatGoesSomewhere: A button that goes somewhere is a link that looks like a button: pass the link component in `as` and the address in `href`.
button.buttonsThatBelongTogetherStand: Buttons that belong together stand 8px apart, the primary one last.
button.onlyIconChangesAnythingA: Only ICON changes anything: a square for a button that is an icon alone.
button.asWideAsItsContainer: As wide as its container, for the one button at the foot of a panel.
button.showsASpinnerAndStops: Shows a spinner and stops further presses.
button.rendersALinkThatLooks: Renders a link that looks like the button.
button.everythingAButtonTakesIs: Everything a <button> takes is passed through.

checkbox.aChoiceAmongSeveralRows: A choice among several: rows to act on, scopes, kinds. For a single on/off use Switch.
checkbox.inATableSFirst: In a table’s first column. `presentational` draws the box only, for a row that is itself the control.
checkbox.whatHappensWhenItIs: What happens when it is pressed.
checkbox.theWordsBesideItA: The words beside it; a node, so a row can keep its own markup.
checkbox.theBoxOnlyWithNo: The box only, with no button of its own.
checkbox.sendACopyToThe: Send a copy to the customer

fields-more.aNumberThatIsNudged: A number that is nudged as often as it is typed: a quantity, a count of days.
fields-more.itStopsAtMinAnd: It stops at `min` and `max` and moves by `step`.
fields-more.theNumberAnEmptyField: The number; an empty field gives an empty string.
fields-more.whereItStopsAndHow: Where it stops and how far a press moves it.
fields-more.whatIsWrongUnderThe: What is wrong, under the field.
fields-more.someoneFromPeoplePickedBy: Someone from People, picked by searching instead of retyping their name and email. A collection field with `admin.component: 'PersonField'` stores the person and fills the fields named in `admin.personFields`.
fields-more.typeANameAnEmail: Type a name, an email or a phone. The chosen person’s contact and the way to People show under it; × unlinks.
fields-more.whichOfTheCollectionS: Which of the collection’s own fields a picked person fills.
fields-more.showsWhoIsLinkedCannot: Shows who is linked; cannot be changed.
fields-more.oneSettingItsNameAnd: One setting: its name and a line about it at the start, its control at the end. Every settings screen is a card of these, so all of them change here.
fields-more.aSwitchANumberA: A switch, a number, a choice
fields-more.theControlIsAsWide: The control is as wide as its kind needs: `AUTO` for a switch, `NARROW` for a number, `FIELD` (the default) for a text or a choice.
fields-more.whatTheControlDoesPer: What the control does, per state, sits behind the ⓘ beside the name. A description too long for its one line is cut and opens from the same ⓘ.
fields-more.widePutsTheControlOn: `wide` puts the control on a line of its own — for a list, a long text, a file with its preview.
fields-more.twoControlsAShortOne: Two controls, a short one, a note
fields-more.severalControlsOfOneSetting: Several controls of one setting stand together at the end in `fc-settings-group`. A number or a short choice sits in `fc-settings-short` (`--narrow` for a number). A remark that belongs to the card, not to one setting, is a `Hint` in `fc-settings-note`.
fields-more.whatTheControlDoesBehind: What the control does, behind the ⓘ.
fields-more.narrowFieldOrAutoHow: NARROW, FIELD or AUTO: how much room the control takes.
fields-more.theControlOnALine: The control on a line of its own.
fields-more.aDayOrADay: A day, or a day and a time, picked from a calendar or typed.
fields-more.minutestepSetsHowFineThe: `minuteStep` sets how fine the minutes are.
fields-more.aTimeIsNotA: A time is not a moment: it carries no day and no zone — opening hours, a daily run.
fields-more.theMomentAsTextNull: The moment as text; null when it is emptied.
fields-more.aDayAMomentOr: A day, a moment, or a time of day alone.
fields-more.nothingIsSentWhileThe: Nothing is sent while the switch is off.
fields-more.accountsMayAddASecond: Accounts may add a second factor to their sign-in.
fields-more.howManyFailedSignIns: How many failed sign-ins lock the account.
fields-more.theLanguageANewVisitor: The language a new visitor sees.
fields-more.everyVisitorPassesABrowser: Every visitor passes a browser check before reaching a site.
fields-more.addressesWhoseForwardedHeadersAre: Addresses whose forwarded headers are believed.
fields-more.aWeeklyCountOfWhat: A weekly count of what the platform runs.
fields-more.howManyEarlierBuildsStay: How many earlier builds stay on disk.

fields-rich.aPictureOrAFile: A picture or a file chosen from the library. Empty, it is a plain square to press — it does not say “no image”.
fields-rich.withHasmanyItIsA: With `hasMany` it is a row of squares with one more to add; they can be put in order.
fields-rich.inARowOfA: In a row of a table
fields-rich.compactIsA32pxSquare: `compact` is a 32px square, the height of a field.
fields-rich.aSquareTheHeightOf: A square the height of a field.
fields-rich.showsTheWholePictureInstead: Shows the whole picture instead of filling the square.
fields-rich.whichKindsOfFileMay: Which kinds of file may be chosen.
fields-rich.aColourAFieldShowing: A colour: a field showing the colour and its value, opening a palette, a picker and the value to type. Plugins may import it as ColorPicker; it is the same control.
fields-rich.notSetAndAColour: Not set, and a colour that is not a hex
fields-rich.theColourAHexFrom: The colour: a hex from the palette or picker, or any colour typed. Empty reads “Not set”.
fields-rich.classesOnTheWrapperThe: Classes on the wrapper; the field fills it.
fields-rich.aListOfShortWords: A list of short words. ChipInputField is free text, each entry a chip. TagField chooses from what a collection already holds, and may add to it.
fields-rich.enterOrACommaEnds: Enter or a comma ends a chip; Backspace on an empty field removes the last one.
fields-rich.aWordNotFoundCan: A word not found can be added.
fields-rich.codeSomeoneEditsJsonCss: Code someone edits: JSON, CSS, a template. For code that is only read, use CodeBlock.
fields-rich.whereAFileIsGiven: Where a file is given. FileDropzone takes ONE file and shows it uploading. DropArea is the target alone, for a page that takes many and lists them itself.
fields-rich.dropareaWhileSomethingIsHeld: DropArea while something is held over it
fields-rich.whatMayBeGivenKinds: What may be given: kinds, size.
fields-rich.whatToDoAndThe: What to do, and the button for those who do not drag.
fields-rich.oneRowOfAGroup: One row of a group that repeats, when each row holds several fields: a raised card with each field’s words on the left of its control, in a column only as wide as the words, and the row’s tools on the right — remove, and the handle that moves it. The handle is dragged, or focused and moved with the arrow keys, so there is no column of arrows. A number in a row is a plain field. VisualMenuField is a menu built from these rows, nested by depth.
fields-rich.theRowsGoInUl: The rows go in `<ul className="fc-repeat__rows">` inside `.fc-repeat`, followed by RepeatRowAdd. In a field, Add moves up to the end of the field’s title line and the rows follow below; a list with its own small heading is wrapped in `.fc-repeat-titled` for the same placement. Tools are `.fc-repeat__tool` buttons, each with a label; two at most stand in a column, so they never make the row taller than its fields.
fields-rich.whenNoFieldHasA: When no field has a label (one line of text, a pair the group heading names), the controls stand side by side.
fields-rich.dragAnItemByIts: Drag an item by its handle, or focus the handle: up and down move it, right nests it under the one above, left moves it back out.
fields-rich.theRowSFieldsEach: The row’s fields, each with its words and its control.
fields-rich.theRowSButtonsRemove: The row’s buttons: remove, then a RepeatRowGrip when the row can move. Two to a column.
fields-rich.howFarTheRowIs: How far the row is nested (24px a level).
fields-rich.reorderingByDraggingTheRow: Reordering by dragging the row (draggable while the pointer is on the grip).
fields-rich.anArrowKeyPressedOn: An arrow key pressed on the handle; answer the row’s new place, and focus follows it.
fields-rich.theAddButtonOfThe: The Add button of the list; on the field’s title line when there is one.
fields-rich.dragToMoveOrUse: Drag to move, or use the arrow keys
fields-rich.label: Label

input.oneLineOfTextEvery: One line of text. Every single-line field in the console is this one, 32px high with 13px text.
input.theLabelStandsAboveThe: The label stands above the field, short, in sentence case.
input.anExampleOfWhatGoes: An example of what goes in — never the label and never the explanation.
input.theFieldTurnsToThe: The field turns to the danger tone and says what is wrong under it.
input.disabledIsNotAvailableNow: Disabled is “not available now”. Read-only is “may be read, may not be changed” and keeps its text colour.
input.anythingANativeInputTakes: Anything a native input takes is passed through: the kind, a pattern, a length.
input.inATableCellOr: In a table cell or a toolbar, where what it is for is already said. Give it an aria-label.
input.whatTheFieldHoldsAnd: What the field holds and what happens when it is typed in.
input.whatIsWrongShownUnder: What is wrong, shown under the field in the danger tone.
input.anExampleOfTheValue: An example of the value, shown while the field is empty.
input.notAvailableMayBeRead: Not available / may be read only.
input.aClassOnTheWrapper: A class on the wrapper / on the field itself. Not for sizes: the height and the text size are the kit’s.
input.everythingANativeInputTakes: Everything a native input takes is passed through.
input.title: Title

motion.howTheConsoleMovesThree: How the console moves. Three durations and one curve, for everything: what was asked for arrives in 200ms, leaves in 150ms, and what answers the pointer takes 150ms. Nothing gets a number of its own. A reader who asked for less motion gets none.
motion.theGroundFadesADialog: The ground fades. A dialog rises 8px and grows from 97%. A sheet comes in from the side it is hinged to. The full-screen modal rises without growing. Each leaves the way it came, a little quicker.
motion.threeThingsInARow: Three things in a row: the button turns to a spinner and stops taking presses; when the save is done the sheet leaves; a toast rises at the corner to say so. A failed save keeps the sheet open and says what is wrong inside it.
motion.theseOpenBesideTheControl: These open beside the control that asked for them, so they travel half as far (4px) and at the pointer’s speed (150ms).
motion.itComesUpFromThe: It comes up from the foot of the screen when something is selected, and goes back down when nothing is.
motion.aButtonDarkensWhileIt: A button darkens while it is held. A checkbox pops and draws its tick. A switch slides. All in 150ms.
motion.aPanelThatIsNot: A panel that is not one of the kit’s overlays takes the class `fc-enter` to arrive like them; `fc-enter--fade` only fades, `fc-enter--menu` is the short, quick one. To leave as well, keep it drawn for the exit with `OverlayPresence` and put `data-state` on it.
motion.somethingThatWasAskedFor: Something that was asked for arrives: a dialog, a sheet, a toast.
motion.whatAnswersThePointerA: What answers the pointer: a hover, a press, a menu, a tooltip.
motion.howFarAnOverlayTravels: How far an overlay travels on its way in.
motion.turnsEveryOneOfThese: Turns every one of these off and leaves the finished state.
motion.title: Title
motion.aPanelOfItsOwn: A panel of its own content.
motion.itBecomesVisibleInThe: It becomes visible in the shop at once.

new-pieces.theConsoleSTypeAs: The console’s type as components. A screen uses these instead of writing a size, a weight or a colour of its own — so the type of every screen changes here.
new-pieces.heading: Heading
new-pieces.threeLevelsH1NamesA: Three levels. h1 names a page or a record, h2 a card, h3 a group inside a card.
new-pieces.smallIsTheConsoleS: `small` is the console’s own size: values, rows, controls.
new-pieces.forAControlThatCarries: For a control that carries no label of its own. A hint explains; as `error` it says what is wrong.
new-pieces.theSizeAndItsLine: The size and its line height.
new-pieces.theMediumWeightTheQuiet: The medium weight; the quiet colour.
new-pieces.theControlItNamesA: The control it names; a quiet word after it.
new-pieces.anExplanationOrWhatIs: An explanation, or what is wrong.
new-pieces.anIconInASmall: An icon in a small tinted square: what kind of thing a row or a card is.
new-pieces.aTipBesideTheFields: A tip beside the fields it explains: a coloured bar, a strong word, a sentence or two. For something about the whole page use Alert.
new-pieces.theStrongWordItStarts: The strong word it starts with.
new-pieces.aSmallPanelThatOpens: A small panel that opens from a control and holds content of its own: a filter, a few fields, a note with an action. For a list of actions use Dropdown.
new-pieces.itClosesOnAPress: It closes on a press outside and on Esc.
new-pieces.whichEdgeOfTheControl: Which edge of the control it lines up with.
new-pieces.itsNameForAScreen: Its name for a screen reader.
new-pieces.aFieldWithAFixed: A field with a fixed part before or after what is typed: a unit, a code, a sign, a domain. The parts are shown, never typed, and never part of the value.
new-pieces.aPartBeforeAfterOr: A part before, after, or both
new-pieces.whatIsTypedWithoutThe: What is typed — without the parts.
new-pieces.theFixedPartsWhatThey: The fixed parts. What they say is the caller’s.
new-pieces.theValueStandsAgainstThe: The value stands against the end, the way a figure is read.
new-pieces.theWordsAboveWhatIs: The words above; what is wrong.
new-pieces.aShortCodeTypedA: A short code typed a character a box — from an authenticator or a message. A pasted code fills every box.
new-pieces.aDashAfterEveryThis: A dash after every this many boxes.
new-pieces.refusedNotAvailableTakesThe: Refused / not available / takes the cursor.
new-pieces.whatTheCodeIsFor: What the code is, for a screen reader.
new-pieces.plusANameOrA: Plus — a name or a value inside text
new-pieces.aHandleIsMadeFrom: A handle is made from the title when left empty.
new-pieces.changingTheHandleBreaksLinks: Changing the handle breaks links that point to the old one.
new-pieces.theCertificateCouldNotBe: The certificate could not be issued.

overlays.whatOpensOverThePage: What opens over the page. A question is a 400px dialog in the middle. A form that edits part of a record is a sheet from the side. Making something new, with room to think, is the focus modal.
overlays.aYesOrNoBefore: A yes-or-no before something that matters. The confirming button says what it does; `variant` makes it the danger button for a removal.
overlays.theDialogItselfForA: The dialog itself, for a question with content of its own. `wide` is for a list to read before answering.
overlays.aPartOfARecord: A part of a record edited beside the page it belongs to, 560px from the side, with Save and Cancel at its foot.
overlays.theWholeScreenForMaking: The whole screen for making something new, in steps when it has them.
overlays.aPictureOverTheWhole: A picture over the whole console: what it is and where it is in the set on top with ✕, ‹ › at the sides when there is more than one. Arrow keys move, Esc closes.
overlays.everyOverlayWhetherItShows: Every overlay: whether it shows, and what closes it (Esc and the backdrop call it too).
overlays.theQuestionAndOneSentence: The question and one sentence about it.
overlays.theAnswerAndTheWords: The answer and the words on the buttons.
overlays.theAnswerIsBeingCarried: The answer is being carried out.
overlays.savingWhatWentWrongA: Saving, what went wrong, a foot of its own.
overlays.stepsAcrossItsHeadAnd: Steps across its head and whether it may be confirmed yet.
overlays.whatTheButtonsWillAct: What the buttons will act on, at the start of the foot: the file chosen.
overlays.aGridOfPicturesRather: A grid of pictures rather than a form: the column takes up to 1120px instead of 720.
overlays.thePicturesWhichOneShows: The pictures, which one shows, moving between them, and what they are.
overlays.aMenuOfActionsThat: A menu of actions that opens from a control — most often a row’s or a card’s ⋯.
overlays.alignedToTheEndSo: Aligned to the end, so it opens inward from the edge of a row or a card.
overlays.theActionsDangerForA: The actions; DANGER for a removal, which goes last.
overlays.whichEdgeOfTheTrigger: Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with.
overlays.theBarThatRisesAt: The bar that rises at the foot of the screen while rows are selected, or while a form has unsaved changes: what is selected, then what can be done with it.
overlays.pressTheButtonToShow: Press the button to show it; its last command clears it.
overlays.whatItSpeaksOf2: What it speaks of: “2 selected”, “Unsaved changes”.
overlays.notAvailableTheWordsFor: Not available; the words for a command that is an icon alone.
overlays.whateverTheQuestionNeedsUnder: Whatever the question needs under it.
overlays.title: Title
overlays.itBecomesVisibleInThe: It becomes visible in the shop at once.
overlays.thisRemovesTheProductAnd: This removes the product and its variants. It cannot be undone.
overlays.theNameShownInThe: The name shown in the list.
overlays.theSiteReturnsToHow: The site returns to how it was on 12 November.
overlays.whatItWillBeAllowed: What it will be allowed to do.

page-header.theHeadOfAPage: The head of a page that is not one list: a settings page, a record that is not a collection’s. A page that IS one list has no page header — its name is the head of its ListShell.
page-header.withALineUnderIt: With a line under it and an action
page-header.withTheWayBackAnd: With the way back and a mark
page-header.aPageOneStepInside: A page one step inside another carries the way back; a thing with an icon of its own shows it as its mark.
page-header.buttonsAtTheEndThe: Buttons at the end, the primary one last.
page-header.theWayBackAsAn: The way back, as an arrow before the name.
page-header.theThingSOwnIcon: The thing’s own icon, in a square before the name.

page-pieces.smallPiecesAScreenWrites: Small pieces a screen writes as a class on its own markup: a folder path, a big figure with its bars, a row of stat cards, a file chip, a picture preview, a link in running text.
page-pieces.stepsSeparatedByASlash: Steps separated by a slash; the current one is `aria-current="page"` and is not a link.
page-pieces.fcFigureAndFcBars: fc-figure and fc-bars — one number and its days
page-pieces.theFigureWithItsUnit: The figure with its unit, and a bar per day; each bar is its share of the highest day, as `height`.
page-pieces.asManyStatcardSAs: As many `StatCard`s as fit, each at least 120px. `fc-stat-strip--tight` is four to a row, two on a phone.
page-pieces.fcFileChipAFile: fc-file-chip — a file named in a line
page-pieces.fcPreviewAPictureInside: fc-preview — a picture inside a card or a sheet
page-pieces.centredOnAQuietGround: Centred on a quiet ground, at most 200px high, never cropped.
page-pieces.fcLinkALinkInside: fc-link — a link inside running text
page-pieces.underlinedInTheTextColour: Underlined in the text colour; a link that is an action is a `Button` instead.
page-pieces.theStepYouAreOn: The step you are on: stronger, not clickable.
page-pieces.fourToARowWith: Four to a row with 8px between, two on a phone.

panels.aPassingMessageAtThe: A passing message at the corner of the screen: something was done, or could not be. It leaves by itself — for something that must stay until dealt with, use Alert.
panels.whatHappenedInAFew: What happened, in a few words, and one sentence more.
panels.oneFigureThePageIs: One figure the page is about, with its name and where it is heading.
panels.withALineUnderThe: With a line under the figure, in columns
panels.columnsLaysCardsSideBy: `Columns` lays cards side by side — two or three — and drops to one column on a narrow screen.
panels.whatIsCountedAndThe: What is counted and the figure, already formatted.
panels.howManyColumnsTopLets: How many columns; `top` lets each be as tall as its own content.
panels.theChangeInPercentAnd: The change, in percent, and whether it is good.
panels.theColourOfTheIcon: The colour of the icon when the figure is good or bad news.
panels.aFewFactsAboutA: A few facts about a thing, each a label over a value, laid out in columns.
panels.aTitledPanelAPlugin: A titled panel a plugin puts on a page that is not its own, with its actions at the end of its head.
panels.withADescriptionAndAn: With a description and an action
panels.thePanelSNameAnd: The panel’s name and a line under it.
panels.buttonsAtTheEndOf: Buttons at the end of the head.
panels.whatHasBeenSentFor: What has been sent for this order.

radio-group.oneChoiceOutOfA: One choice out of a few, all of them on screen at once.
radio-group.eachChoiceInABox: Each choice in a box of its own, the chosen one outlined — for a choice that decides what the rest of the form is.
radio-group.theWholeGroupOrOne: The whole group, or one option (see “No products” above).
radio-group.theChosenValueAndWhat: The chosen value and what happens on a choice.
radio-group.whatIsBeingChosenAlso: What is being chosen; also the group’s accessible name.
radio-group.eachChoiceInItsOwn: Each choice in its own box.
radio-group.boxesSideBySideWhere: Boxes side by side where there is room.
radio-group.theWholeGroupIsNot: The whole group is not available.
radio-group.theSameSumOffEvery: The same sum off every order.
radio-group.aShareOfTheOrder: A share of the order’s total.

search-field.theSearchOverAList: The search over a list. It gives the text as it is typed; the list decides what it matches.
search-field.onceItHoldsTextIt: Once it holds text it shows a control to empty it.
search-field.itIsAsWideAs: It is as wide as what holds it.
search-field.theTextAndWhatHappens: The text and what happens as it is typed.
search-field.takesTheCursorWhenIt: Takes the cursor when it appears.
search-field.forItsPlaceInA: For its place in a row (its width), never its look.

select.oneChoiceOutOfA: One choice out of a list that is too long, or too rarely changed, to lay out as radios.
select.thePlaceholderSaysWhatIs: The placeholder says what is to be chosen.
select.forAListLongEnough: For a list long enough to need finding in. The search is inside the menu.
select.whenNoneIsAValid: When “none” is a valid answer, the field can be emptied again.
select.oneQuietLineAtThe: One quiet line at the foot of the menu, for what the list leaves out.
select.withOncreateoptionWhateverIsTyped: With `onCreateOption` whatever is typed and not found can be added from the menu.
select.theChosenOptionSValue: The chosen option’s value and what happens on a choice.
select.aSearchAtTheHead: A search at the head of the menu.
select.forOptionsFetchedAsThe: For options fetched as the search is typed.
select.aLineAtTheFoot: A line at the foot of the menu.
select.letsAMissingOptionBe: Lets a missing option be added from the menu.
select.putsARemoveControlOn: Puts a remove control on each option.

shell.theConsoleSSideMenu: The console’s side menu, built from the same pieces the real one renders: its head, its rows, the way back out of Settings, and the account at its foot.
shell.theHeadHoldsTheSite: The head holds the site, the control that folds the menu and the notifications. The open page’s row is raised.
shell.aSectionWithPagesUnder: A section with pages under it
shell.aSectionSPagesHang: A section’s pages hang under its row while it is open: the rows it declares, one level, and nothing else. Its other pages are reached from the pages they belong to and from the big search (⌘K) — the menu never goes three deep and never changes with the page that is open.
shell.settingsIsAPlaceOf: Settings is a place of its own: the way back first, then its pages.
shell.theWayOutOfA: The way out of a place with its own menu.
shell.twoSearchesTheOneIn: Two searches. The one in the menu narrows the menu’s rows as it is typed. ⌘K opens the big one over the page, which finds a page from anywhere.
shell.arrowKeysMoveEnterOpens: Arrow keys move, Enter opens, Esc closes.
shell.whatMatchesHintIsA: What matches; `hint` is a quiet word at the row’s end.
shell.theFieldSWordsWhat: The field’s words; what it says with no match.
shell.whatTheBellOpensWhat: What the bell opens: what happened while nobody looked, unread first.
shell.aPluginIsWaitingFor: A plugin is waiting for approval

small.aKeyOrKeysTo: A key, or keys, to press.
small.theKeyAsItIs: The key as it is printed on a keyboard.
small.aHairlineBetweenTwoThings: A hairline between two things that belong to one whole.
small.betweenControlsOnOneLine: Between controls on one line; it takes the line’s height.
small.theShapeOfWhatIs: The shape of what is still loading, so the page does not jump when it arrives.
small.itsSizeANumberIs: Its size; a number is pixels.
small.howFarSomethingThatTakes: How far something that takes a while has got: a download, an upload, an import.
small.forAMeasureRatherThan: For a measure rather than a wait: the tone says it needs looking at.
small.withoutAValueTheBar: Without a value the bar runs on its own: it says only that the thing is going.
small.n0100LeftOutWhen: 0–100; left out when the length is not known.
small.howFarInTheCaller: How far, in the caller’s words.
small.saysTheFigureIsHigh: Says the figure is high: a disk nearly full, a limit nearly reached.
small.oneThingShownByIts: One thing shown by its picture: a file, a folder. Pressing the picture opens it; everything that can be done with it is in its menu, so nothing waits for a pointer to hover.
small.aPictureAFileWithout: A picture, a file without one, a folder
small.theyStandInFcTile: They stand in `fc-tile-grid`, which fits as many as the width holds.
small.theThingSNameCut: The thing’s name, cut with an ellipsis when it is longer than the tile.
small.oneQuietLineUnderThe: One quiet line under the name.
small.thePictureSAddressWithout: The picture’s address; without one the icon stands in its place.
small.aVideoSAddressDrawn: A video’s address, drawn as its first frame where a picture would stand.
small.drawnWhenThereIsNo: Drawn when there is no picture.
small.badgesOnThePictureWhat: Badges on the picture: what the thing is marked as.
small.chosenTheTileIsOutlined: Chosen: the tile is outlined and its tick stays.
small.givenTheTileCarriesA: Given, the tile carries a tick.
small.whatCanBeDoneWith: What can be done with the thing.
small.whatPressingThePictureDoes: What pressing the picture does, for a reader who cannot see it.
small.thePicturesOfOneThing: The pictures of one thing as a card: the chosen one large, the rest in a strip under it. With no pictures the card is not drawn.
small.aSmallPictureMakesIt: A small picture makes it the large one; the large one asks the page to open it full size.
small.noStripThereIsNothing: No strip: there is nothing to choose between.
small.whatThePicturesShowFor: What the pictures show, for a reader who cannot see them.
small.theLargePictureWasPressed: The large picture was pressed; the page owns the full-size view.
small.aSpinnerWithAWord: A spinner with a word, for a wait with no shape to draw.
small.somethingHappeningRightHereInline: Something happening right here, inline: beside a word, in a badge, in a field. It takes the colour of the text around it. A button that is working uses its own `isLoading`; a part of a page still loading is `Loader`.
small.theButtonKeepsItsIcon: The button keeps its icon until it works, then the spinner takes the icon’s place and the words stay.
small.n12pxInsteadOf16pxFor: 12px instead of 16px, for a badge or small text.
small.whatIsHappeningForA: What is happening, for a screen reader.
small.aValueSomeoneCopiesElsewhere: A value someone copies elsewhere — an id, an email, a tracking number — with a copy button after it.
small.childrenIsWhatIsShown: `children` is what is shown; `value` is what is copied.
small.codeToReadAndCopy: Code to read and copy. For code someone edits, use CodeEditor.
small.aFileNameOrA: A file name or a language, in a head over the code.
small.whatStandsWhereAList: What stands where a list or a card has nothing: what is missing, why, and the way to fill it.
small.onOneLineForAn: On one line, for an empty part inside a card that holds other things.
small.aQuietIconOverThe: A quiet icon over the title.
small.oneLineInsteadOfA: One line instead of a centred block.
small.nothingMatchesTheFiltersIn: Nothing matches the filters in force.

surfaces.theSurfaceThingsStandOn: The surface things stand on. RecordCard is the card of a record’s page: a head of fixed height (name, count, something beside it, its ⋯) and a body. Card is the bare surface.
surfaces.withACountSomethingBeside: With a count, something beside the name and a menu
surfaces.aBandOfItsOwn: A band of its own under the head: what narrows the list at the start, what works on it at the end.
surfaces.theBareSurfaceWithOr: The bare surface, with or without its own padding.
surfaces.actionsStandAtTheEnd: `actions` stand at the end of the card’s title line — a quiet button that works on what the card shows.
surfaces.theCardSNameWithout: The card’s name. Without one there is no head.
surfaces.aFigureBesideTheName: A figure beside the name; 0 is shown, null is not.
surfaces.whatStandsBetweenTheName: What stands between the name and the ⋯.
surfaces.theContentBringsItsOwn: The content brings its own padding.
surfaces.buttonsAtTheEndOf: Buttons at the end of the card’s title line.
surfaces.aListAsOneCard: A list as one card: its name and actions in the head, what narrows it and what searches it in a band, the table from edge to edge, a foot. Every list in the console stands in this.
surfaces.nameActionsTabsSearchAnd: Name, actions, tabs, search and a table
surfaces.withALineUnderThe: With a line under the name and a foot
surfaces.listshellheadIsTheHeadBy: ListShellHead is the head by itself, for a list that builds its own bands between the head and the table.
surfaces.theHeadTheNameHow: The head: the name, how many, a line under it.
surfaces.buttonsAtTheEndOf2: Buttons at the end of the head, the primary one last.
surfaces.startOfTheBandTabs: Start of the band: Tabs or a Filters button.
surfaces.endOfTheBandThe: End of the band: the search, the order.
surfaces.theListItselfEdgeTo: The list itself, edge to edge.
surfaces.theOneTableOneLine: The one table. One line a row, 48px; sortable heads, selection, row actions, pages. Below 768px of its own width each row becomes a card.
surfaces.aCellIsPlainText: A cell is plain text unless it needs more. `fc-dt-strong` is the row’s name, `fc-dt-quiet` a second fact, `fc-dt-who` a person with their initial. The column with `className: 'fc-dt-fill'` takes the spare width and cuts its text; add `fc-dt-wrap` to let it run onto more lines.
surfaces.aBoxAtTheStart: A box at the start of each row and one for all of them in the head. Pair it with CommandBar.
surfaces.onrowclickMakesTheWholeRow: `onRowClick` makes the whole row the way into the record; `actions` puts its controls at the end, where they stay while the table scrolls sideways.
surfaces.aColumnWithSortableGets: A column with `sortable` gets an arrow; the table says which sort is asked for and the page fetches it. With `totalDocs`, `limit` and `page` the foot shows the count and the pages.
surfaces.theColumnsAccessorIsA: The columns. `accessor` is a key of the row or a function giving the cell.
surfaces.controlsAtTheEndOf: Controls at the end of each row.
surfaces.theFootTheCountAnd: The foot: the count and the pages.
surfaces.whatItSaysWithNo: What it says with no rows.
surfaces.columnsAndActionsThatStay: Columns and actions that stay while it scrolls sideways.
surfaces.rowsBecomeCardsWhenThe: Rows become cards when the table is narrow.
surfaces.aListOfInstalledOr: A list of installed or named things — plugins, themes, people — where each row is a thing with its state and its controls, not a line of columns.
surfaces.whatStandsBeforeTheIcon: What stands before the icon: a tick, when rows can be chosen.
surfaces.whatStandsBeforeTheName: What stands before the name: an icon, or a person’s initial.
surfaces.theNameAndTheStates: The name and the states beside it.
surfaces.oneLineUnderTheName: One line under the name; `failed` turns it to the danger tone.
surfaces.aQuietFactBeforeThe: A quiet fact before the controls; hidden on a phone.
surfaces.whatTheCardSaysWith: What the card says with no rows.
surfaces.theBarOverAPage: The bar over a page’s content when that content is not one list card: what narrows it at the start, the search and the page’s action at the end.
surfaces.aWholePageWithNothing: A whole page with nothing to show: not found, not allowed, failed to load.
surfaces.anIconOverTheTitle: An icon over the title; the ways out under it.
surfaces.aCardWithNoName: A card with no name is body only.
surfaces.aTitleAndALine: A title and a line under it.
surfaces.whatThisPluginRunsAnd: What this plugin runs and has registered.
surfaces.walletsGiftCardsAndThe: Wallets, gift cards and the transaction ledger.
surfaces.itMayHaveBeenDeleted: It may have been deleted, or the address is wrong.

switch.aSingleThingThatIs: A single thing that is on or off, in force the moment it is flipped. For a choice among several use Checkbox.
switch.oneLineUnderTheLabel: One line under the label for what flipping it does.
switch.atTheEndOfA: At the end of a row that already names the thing.
switch.whatHappensWhenItIs: What happens when it is flipped; may be async.
switch.letsCustomersPayWithA: Lets customers pay with a gift card at checkout.

tabs.partsOfOnePageOne: Parts of one page, one shown at a time. Tabs have the control’s corner (6px), never a pill.
tabs.asAFilterOverA: As a filter over a list or a switch inside a card.
tabs.withIconsAndADisabled: With icons and a disabled tab
tabs.variantBarIsTheRow: `variant="bar"` is the row under a page’s header: full width with a line under it. A tab marked `end` stands at the far side.
tabs.theSecondLevelIsVariant: The second level is `variant="second"` directly under the bar. It starts on the same edge, 12px under the bar and 16px over what it opens; when the tabs do not fit a line they wrap.
tabs.theTabsEndSendsA: The tabs. `end` sends a tab to the far side of a bar.
tabs.theOpenTabAndWhat: The open tab and what happens on a choice.
tabs.thePageSOwnRow: The page’s own row / the level under it.
tabs.theAccessibleNameOfThe: The accessible name of the row.
tabs.theStepsOfSomethingFilled: The steps of something filled in over several screens, each showing how far it has got.
tabs.eachStepAndHowFar: Each step and how far it is: 'not-started', 'in-progress' or 'completed'.
tabs.theOpenStepAndWhat: The open step and what happens on a choice.

text-area.textThatRunsToMore: Text that runs to more than a line: a description, a note.
text-area.howTallItStartsIs: How tall it starts is `rows`; it can still be dragged taller.
text-area.whatItHoldsAndWhat: What it holds and what happens when it is typed in.
text-area.whatIsWrongUnderThe: What is wrong, under the field.
text-area.everythingANativeTextArea: Everything a native text area takes is passed through.
text-area.anythingTheNextPersonShould: Anything the next person should know

tooltip.aFewWordsThatAppear: A few words that appear over a thing on hover, on focus, and on a tap on a phone. For what an icon means or what a cut text says in full — never for something the reader must see.
tooltip.onABadgeOrA: On a badge or a word
tooltip.aboveByDefaultUnderWhen: Above by default; under when there is no room above, or when asked.
tooltip.whatItSaysKeepIt: What it says. Keep it to a line or two.
tooltip.whatChangedSinceItWas: What changed since it was approved: +database +api
tooltip.stockKeepingUnitTheShop: Stock keeping unit: the shop’s own code for the product.

record-pieces.valueRowIntro: One fact of a record: its name, its value, and an optional small action at the end. The same row a saved record draws, so a plugin's values read like the console's own.
record-pieces.aControlAtTheEnd: A control at the end of the row
record-pieces.mutedForAnAbsentValue: Drawn muted, for a value that says it is absent
record-pieces.crumbsIntro: Where a page sits: a back button to its list, then list › page.
record-pieces.theListThePageBelongsTo: The list the page belongs to

parts-line.intro: A whole told as its parts on one quiet line, under the thing it describes: where an order line's units came from, which accounts a payment was split across.
parts-line.oneSourceText: With one part the line still says where it is: a single warehouse is told the same way as several.
parts-line.noDetailText: Each part shows only what it has; nothing stands in for a missing detail.
parts-line.inALineText: Its place: under the name of the thing it describes, beside other quiet details.
parts-line.optParts: The parts, in the order they are read. None: nothing is drawn, caption included.
parts-line.optDetail: A short qualifier after the label, quieter than it.
parts-line.optCount: How many of the whole this part holds, printed ×n.
parts-line.optHref: Makes the label a link to the part's own record.
parts-line.optCaption: A word before the parts saying what they are.
parts-line.optClass: Places the line; it never restyles it.

record-summary-row.intro: A record too big for a card — an order's stored data, a block of metadata, a payload — told as ONE row: how many values it holds and what is in it, opening the values in a drawer beside the page. Reach for it whenever a card could be handed an object of unknown size; nothing a card is given can then run the page to thousands of pixels.
record-summary-row.title: Order record
record-summary-row.name: Name
record-summary-row.basic: One row that opens a drawer
record-summary-row.basicText: The whole row is the button. Its text is the count; the card's own heading says what the record is.
record-summary-row.named: Name and count on the row
record-summary-row.namedText: Without a card heading above it, the row carries the name itself, with the count as a quiet pill.
record-summary-row.automaticText: A read-only json field is told this way on its own once it holds more than 12 values. The keys the plugin named come first, in its words.
record-summary-row.unnamedText: Without a vocabulary every key is drawn under a humanised name. With one, the keys it does not name follow under Technical, with their count, so an untranslated key is visible and never mixed in.
record-summary-row.small: A small record stays in the card
record-summary-row.smallText: Twelve values or fewer fit one screen, so they are read where they stand — no drawer to open.
record-summary-row.optTitle: What the record is called: the drawer's title, and the row's text unless rowText is given.
record-summary-row.optRowText: What the row says in place of title, when the card's heading already names the record. The count pill is then not drawn.
record-summary-row.optCountLabel: The count in words (166 values). The caller supplies it so the row speaks the console's language.
record-summary-row.optCount: How many values it holds, for a caller that wants the number itself.
record-summary-row.optHint: One short line at the row's end saying what is inside. Never a value. Hidden on a phone.
record-summary-row.optSubtitle: One quiet line under the drawer's title.
record-summary-row.optChildren: The values, drawn inside the drawer. Anything: fact rows, a structured value, a table.
record-summary-row.optClass: Places the row; it never restyles it.

qr-code.intro: A value — a link, a SKU, a box number — drawn as a QR code a phone can read. On screen it is this component; on a printed label it is the same drawing as SVG markup.
qr-code.aLinkText: Scanning it opens the address. A product, a box or a place in a warehouse gets one this way.
qr-code.withCaptionText: One short line under the code says what it is.
qr-code.forPrintText: QrCode.svg gives the same code as markup with a size in any CSS unit, for label sheets and box labels.
qr-code.emptyText: It renders nothing, so a record without a code never shows an empty square.
qr-code.optValue: What the code holds. Keep it short: a link or an identifier, not a description.
qr-code.optSize: Edge length in pixels, quiet zone included.
qr-code.optTitle: The accessible name; the value when not given.
qr-code.optClass: For its place in a layout, never its look.
qr-code.optSvg: The same code as SVG markup, for a page that is printed.

scan.intro: Reads a barcode or a QR code with the camera and hands back the text in it. Nothing leaves the browser; where there is no camera the code is typed, or comes from a keyboard scanner.
scan.dialogText: Opening it starts the rear camera. The first code read closes the camera and is handed back. Below the picture the code can be typed instead.
scan.inSearchText: Given onScan, SearchField ends in a scan button. The code read becomes the search and onScan decides what opens.
scan.ownTitleText: Say what is being scanned when it is not a search.
scan.scanBoxText: The QR code on the box label.
scan.optOpen: Whether it is open, and how it closes. The camera runs only while it is open.
scan.optResult: The code read, trimmed. Called once per opening.
scan.optTitle: The heading; "Scan a code" when not given.
scan.optOnScan: On SearchField: turns on the scan button and receives the code after onChange.

label-sheet.intro: Prints labels — product stickers, box labels, shelf tags — on A4, laid out the way label paper is. Each label is markup the caller writes; the sheet places it and opens the print dialog.
label-sheet.a4x24Text: 70 × 37 mm, three across: the common product-sticker paper. Fine on plain paper too — the dashed lines are for cutting.
label-sheet.a4x10Text: 105 × 57 mm, two across: big enough to read across a room, for boxes.
label-sheet.ownText: Give the columns, rows and label size of the paper in the drawer.
label-sheet.optPrint: Lays the labels out page by page and opens the print dialog; the page is removed afterwards.
label-sheet.optHtml: The same document as a string, for a preview.
label-sheet.optLayouts: The common A4 papers: 24 stickers, 10 box labels, one label per page.
label-sheet.optGrid: How many labels across and down one page.
label-sheet.optCut: Dashed cut lines around each label.
label-sheet.optEscape: Makes text safe to put into a label. Everything the caller did not write itself goes through it.

page.everyComponentOfTheConsole: Every component of the console. Open one to see each way it is used, the code for it and the options it takes.
